about: FROZEN Deep test split (2026-10-23). Written blind to how the system behaves: no acceptance run, export or report was read. Labels were written from my own knowledge of the five English books in the books corpus (Pride and Prejudice, Adventures of Sherlock Holmes, Frankenstein, Alice, The Time Machine) BEFORE the corpus text was reopened; the lexical audit is evals/deep/test_audit.json. 10 answerable items that each need two or more separate passages (two stories or two books for deep-test-sherlock-two-stepfathers and deep-test-cross-two-elizabeths) and 6 should-decline lookalikes. Mention fields: mention_all = strings the answer must all contain; mention = any-of alternatives. Not edited after the third commit: no label, threshold or prompt changes because of how this set scores.

turns: Which Bennet sister turns down Mr. Collins's proposal, and which of her friends accepts him within three days?
items.proof: Label written from my own knowledge of the book BEFORE the corpus text was reopened (audit afterwards). Elizabeth refuses Collins at Longbourn (vol. 1, ch. 19) and Charlotte Lucas accepts him days later (ch. 22). Two chapters apart.

turns: What is the name of Mr. Darcy's estate in Derbyshire, and of the Hertfordshire house that Mr. Bingley rents?
items.proof: Label written from my own knowledge of the book BEFORE the corpus text was reopened (audit afterwards). Pemberley (Darcy, Derbyshire; the Elizabeth/Gardiners visit) and Netherfield Park (Bingley's rented house near Meryton). Different places, far apart in the book.

turns: Two Sherlock Holmes clients are victims of a villainous stepfather: in one story the stepfather poses as his stepdaughter's suitor, in the other he keeps a cheetah and a baboon. Name both stepfathers.
items.proof: Label written from my own knowledge of the book BEFORE the corpus text was reopened (audit afterwards). A Case of Identity: James Windibank poses as Hosmer Angel. The Speckled Band: Dr. Grimesby Roylott keeps a cheetah and a baboon. Two stories.

turns: Who stole the blue carbuncle from the Countess of Morcar, and who is the owner of the hat and goose that the commissionaire Peterson found on Christmas morning?
items.proof: Label written from my own knowledge of the book BEFORE the corpus text was reopened (audit afterwards). The Blue Carbuncle: James Ryder (the hotel attendant) stole the stone; the lost hat and goose are Henry Baker's. Opening and closing of one story.

turns: What work does the Red-Headed League pay Jabez Wilson to do each day, and what was the League really a cover for?
items.proof: Label written from my own knowledge of the book BEFORE the corpus text was reopened (audit afterwards). The Red-Headed League: copying out the Encyclopaedia Britannica; the scheme was to keep Wilson away from his pawnbroker's shop while a tunnel was dug to the City and Suburban Bank's vault. Opening vs. Holmes's explanation.

turns: Which servant of the Frankenstein family is hanged for William's murder, and what item found in her pocket is taken as proof against her?
items.proof: Label written from my own knowledge of the book BEFORE the corpus text was reopened (audit afterwards). Justine Moritz; the miniature picture William wore (the creature plants it). The murder scene and the trial are far apart.
